# 油價重挫、Meta專案債上漲，Nvidia信用風險卻升高

## 能源降溫帶動債券，實質借款成本仍未下降

美國暫停對伊朗空襲，週一布蘭特原油大跌9.07%至$88，美債延續反彈。10年期殖利率降4個基點至4.65%，幅度超過2年期的2個基點，後者收4.31%。這次由長端領漲，與週五短端較強的情況相反，2s10s收窄至34個基點。

但油價回落沒有帶來更低的實質殖利率。10年期通膨補償下降5個基點至2.21%，已超過名目殖利率跌幅，實質殖利率反而微升至2.44%。即使幾乎所有受訪經濟學家都預期聯準會維持利率，交換市場仍給予7月升息接近40%的機率。投資人降低了部分能源風險定價，對政策與資金成本的疑慮卻未消失。

兩筆AI相關交易凸顯這種差異。Sopaipilla的$125.5億Meta資料中心融資，以7.534%殖利率定價後上漲，用明顯讓利完成前一日仍有疑慮的發行。Nvidia的5年期違約保障成本，卻因潛在保證與客戶融資受到檢視，最多上升14個基點至82個基點。買方願意在適當價格承接有支持的專案，同時也要求更高補償，以承擔AI網絡中其他公司的義務最終落到大型贊助者身上的風險。

## 通膨補償降得比美債殖利率更快

美國在近兩週空襲後暫停攻擊，伊朗連續第三天未報復，阿曼也參與恢復荷莫茲航運的協商，WTI下跌8.05%至$82.12。但華府警告，談判失敗可能恢復攻擊，航運復甦仍有條件。即使經過週一跌幅，布蘭特一個月仍上漲22.24%，WTI上漲18.62%。

美債漲幅由短端向中長端擴大。5年期殖利率降3個基點至4.40%，10年期與30年期各降4個基點至4.65%、5.12%。2s10s與2s30s都收窄2個基點，分別為34與81個基點。2、5、10、30年期殖利率整週仍各升10、7、5、1個基點，一個月升幅則為24、28、27、25個基點。

抗通膨債顯示，這次反彈高度依賴油價。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降5個基點，幅度比週五的2個基點更大；實質殖利率卻升1個基點至2.44%，比一週前高9個基點、比一個月前高26個基點。通膨補償下降，尚未讓債券持有人降低要求的實質報酬。

7月28至29日聯準會會議前，經濟學家與交易員的看法仍有落差。7月14日公布的6月CPI，出現六年來首次下跌，當時7月升息機率約10%，如今接近40%。花旗短率交易員對維持利率有高度信心；但就業穩定、關稅已生效，以及能源再度上漲的風險，仍支持較早行動的主張。

主席Kevin Warsh減少前瞻指引，使結果更難預測。Citadel Securities認為，意外升息可建立真正依數據決策的可信度，並在通膨根深蒂固前影響薪資與定價。其他策略師則預期維持利率，但先為9月鋪路，市場也已完全計入9月前升息。油價下跌支持等待，卻還不足以確定官員何時會回應更廣泛的通膨風險。

週一標售顯示，不同年期的需求並不一致。近期殖利率提高後，$690億2年期券獲穩健買盤；5年期標售卻較弱，得標殖利率高於市場預期。這使週二$440億7年期標售更受矚目，投資人須在更長持有期間中評估政策變數。短券賣得順利，不代表曲線更遠處也有同樣需求。

部分機構已利用較高殖利率延長存續期間。State Street旗下管理$6兆資產的部門，戰術上轉向較長天期債券與信用債，即使已放棄原先2026年10年期殖利率降至約3.5%的預測。新版基本情境是聯準會今年不動，待成長放慢後於2027年初寬鬆。這種配置先取得利息收入、等待景氣降溫，而不是押注政策立即轉向。

週一改善了長債市值，卻沒有抹平先前損失。長天期美債指數上漲0.62%，一個月仍跌3.72%；30年期殖利率同期仍高25個基點。政府借款與長天期企業債供給，持續爭取能夠承受期間波動的資金。

## Sopaipilla掛牌走強，Nvidia的CDS卻急升

Sopaipilla從訂單偏薄，推進到完成發行並在次級市場上漲。BlackRock相關特殊目的公司為Meta艾爾帕索園區發行$125.5億投資級債，殖利率7.534%，較美債高287.5個基點。規模比最初預期增加約$2.73億，但$200億訂單仍僅涵蓋1.6倍，今年投資級發行平均約4倍，且交易在銷售過程中未能收窄定價。

初期交易利差隨後降至約260個基點，比發行收窄約27.5個基點。新券原本比類似的Beignet資料中心債多提供約40個基點。Sopaipilla持有專案80%，Meta持有20%，本金分期攤還，Meta租約支持付款。保障結構搭配較高殖利率，在薄訂單之後仍吸引買盤，但發行成本明顯高於單看投資級評等可能預期的水準。

Nvidia信用保障走向相反。5年期CDS最多上升14個基點至82個基點，為11月開始活躍交易以來最大增幅。逾$7,500億潛在AI安排的討論，包括可能為最多$2,500億OpenAI算力租約提供保證，以及可能融資$3,500億晶片採購。這些仍是潛在承諾，不是已完成借款，投資人卻已開始評估多少客戶風險可能轉移給Nvidia。

較強的贊助者可透過保證，降低信用較弱對手方的資金成本。先前Broadcom支持$350億Anthropic融資中的大部分義務，便提供了比較。保證有助擴大買方、提高評等，但客戶現金流不如預期時，支持者也會承擔損失。在Meta支持的現券上漲當天，Nvidia的CDS正反映市場對這類義務的疑慮。

傳統企業仍能在其他市場取得大額資金。AT&T以四筆4至19年期歐元券，加上一筆£5.5億、26年期英鎊券，共募集約€47億等值資金，為至少2014年以來，這段季節性清淡期間首筆五分券歐洲交易。銷售過程利差最多收窄30個基點，4年期最終為交換利率加65個基點，最長歐元券加175個基點；9.5至19.1個基點新券讓利，有助完成配置。

相較夏季發行日程，AT&T規模尤其醒目。前一週歐洲企業、金融與主權相關發行合計僅約€50億，當週調查預估也只有€20億至€50億。2026年美國企業赴歐發債已達€1,150億，尋求較低總殖利率與更廣買方。即使季節性交易清淡，願意讓利的成熟企業仍有歐洲需求可用。

US Renal Care的貸款人要求的不只是價格，還包括拿回擔保品。公司考慮約$20億再融資，將2023年債務管理交易中移出原債權人可追索範圍的資產歸還。擬議方案包括$12億第一順位貸款、利差約基準加500個基點；$6.4億第一順位票據、票息約8%；以及$3.5億第二順位票據、約11%至12%。貸款及次順位票據將折價發行。

先前交易移走約三分之一資產。如今營運改善，定期貸款報價也從3月底94美分升至約98，帶來再融資機會。但政府醫療給付風險及有限自由現金流仍在，方案也未必成行。在高利率下延長到期年限，歸還擔保品已成為談判條件之一。

市政債在經歷2025年4月以來最差的一週後，也出現相對價值機會。10年期AAA殖利率接近同年期美債的71%，為3月以來最便宜比率。先前免稅收入需求強勁、推高債價，這波跌勢回吐了部分溢價。

企業債內部的分散效果則變差。凱雷估算，投資級債與美股的相關係數，從2010至2020年平均0.13，升至2020年以來0.63，前100大發行人約占市場65%。資產擔保融資可透過消費貸款、設備租賃等帶來不同收入來源，並由次順位資本先承擔損失，但保障是否有效，仍取決於授信品質與結構。

債券基金溫和回升：LQD漲0.26%、HYG漲0.05%、JNK漲0.07%，一個月仍各跌2.73%、0.70%、0.79%。美債反彈有利報酬，但更有資訊量的信用變化，是Sopaipilla完成發行所需的價格、Nvidia的潛在義務，以及US Renal Care的擔保品談判。

## 油價下降，各央行卻沒有共同答案

德國與英國10年期殖利率隨油價各降4、5個基點，ECB管委Peter Kazimir卻仍主張至少再升息一次。他認為，中東局勢即使稍微改善，也不會消除能源的完整影響或第二輪效應風險；除非數據格外有說服力，否則不會放棄9月升息，衝突再升級甚至可能需要未來幾季多次調升。ECB前次維持利率後，市場已完全計入9月升息25個基點。

瑞士的政策基本情境溫和得多。SNB內部預期，在沒有新衝擊下，利率可維持0%至2027年底；目前通膨0.5%，預估高點0.8%，都在0%至2%目標內。市場卻給予約50%的12月升息機率，並完全計入3月前升息。能源與匯率風險，使交易價格比央行通膨預測更鷹。

日本超長債仍接近紀錄殖利率。40年期前一週達4.01%，對照5月高點4.355%；日圓在164兌$1附近。通膨持續、赤字前景及日本銀行減少購債，共同壓抑需求。首相高市早苗支持率下降，也增加政府可能進一步擴大支出或減稅的疑慮。

不過，高殖利率開始吸引不同看法。Azimut認為，通膨低於2%，使現有水準的長天期日本公債具有吸引力。財務大臣片山皋月也已呼籲，管理$1.81兆資產的政府退休金投資基金及其他大型退休基金增加國內配置。更強的本土買盤可穩定日本公債，同時卻可能留住原本流向美債的資金。日本債券需求改善，不一定等於日本對美債需求增加。

新加坡沒有等待油價回落後再判斷。金管局連續第二次提高匯率政策區間斜率，允許新加坡元加快升值。核心通膨僅1.6%，但正產出缺口擴大至潛在GDP的0.7%，加上電價上漲，當局預期7月起壓力增加，新加坡元上漲0.15%。相較印尼與馬來西亞維持傳統政策利率，共同能源衝擊緩和之後，各國依然採取不同回應。

## 印尼的政策震盪，壓過外部環境改善

印尼央行總裁Perry Warjiyo提前兩年辭職，使印尼未能跟上新興市場債券的有利走勢。資深副總裁Destry Damayanti代理，印尼盾最多跌0.3%、股市最多跌0.8%，10年期公債殖利率升4個基點。印尼美元債違約保障變貴，同時亞洲不含日本多數投資級CDS卻因美伊緊張緩和，出現一個月來最大跌幅。

Warjiyo任內5月以來已多次干預匯市、累計升息100個基點，印尼盾仍接近紀錄低點。新法把成長與就業納入央行職責，政府又要求支持8%成長目標，此時總裁離任，使獨立性更受關注。先前已將主權展望改為負向的惠譽警告，若市場認為央行獨立性減弱，可能提高借款成本、侵蝕外部緩衝。油價下跌不足以抵銷這些制度疑慮。

巴基斯坦較有空間受惠於能源降溫。央行依20位受訪經濟學家中19位的預期，維持11.5%，當時通膨已從兩年高點開始下降。標普升評至B、展望穩定，支持市場信心，央行預估2027財政年度成長3.5%至4.5%。但該國逾90%能源需求經由荷莫茲運送，復甦仍暴露在航運再度受阻的風險中。

央行預估到2027年6月，通膨接近5%至7%目標區間上緣；另一項調查較不樂觀，預期2027財政年度通膨8.5%、成長4%。維持利率，讓央行能等待進口燃料成本下降是否持久的更多證據。

智利7月28日決策前，市場已計入明顯政策轉向。政策利率4.5%，2年期利率卻在21天上升47個基點至4.79%。交換市場從預期降息25個基點，改為12個月內至少升息一次；1年損益兩平通膨率一週升約30個基點至3.41%，一個月累計升123個基點。6月CPI為4.3%，高於前值3.9%及預估4.1%，通膨壓力早於最新油價變化。

智利仍成功發行€31億8、12、20年期債券，最終利差為交換利率加100、120、143個基點，明顯低於初步指引。但供給還會增加：國會批准額外$62億借款，財政部計畫2026年剩餘期間發行$52億國際債。預估債務2029年達GDP的44.2%高點，接近45%審慎上限，也接近部分分析師認為可能引發降評的水準。

委內瑞拉債權人持續整合，重整路線圖卻仍延遲。1月以來逾15家基金加入委員會，目標掌握約$600億違約主權及國營石油公司債的一半；該團體2024年持有量已逾$100億。2027年債券今年上漲逾60%後，接近50美分，也逼近許多回收估值，但主權方尚未提出與債權人協調相應的方案。

巴西的高利息收入也伴隨財政問題。Selic為14.25%、接近二十年高點，稅負及債務比率又高於許多新興市場同儕。XP創辦人警告，赤字若不修正，終將以通膨與更高利率形式回來。即使平台有BRL1.5兆客戶資產，淨流入仍年減39%，反映高名目殖利率之下，投資人依舊承壓。

整體外部環境改善，EMB上漲0.34%，長天期新興市場美元主權債指數漲0.56%。美元近乎持平，油價及美債殖利率下降有利多數借款人；印尼反向走勢則顯示，本地政策公信力可迅速壓過這些利多。

## 油價大跌，科技股仍落後

多數美股上漲，主要指數卻幾乎未受惠於便宜能源。S&P 500漲0.02%，Nasdaq 100跌0.32%，半導體跌2.23%，VIX升0.48%至18.67%。AI支出及融資疑慮未退，與信用市場對保證和未來債務供給的檢視同時發生。

美元指數微升0.06%至101.53，對海外借款人沒有增加太多單日壓力。黃金在油價重挫之際仍漲0.16%，反映談判與航運未定。市場歡迎局勢降溫，卻未將其視為已完成的和解；科技跌勢也使名目殖利率下降，未能帶來全面風險資產上漲。

## 商品急跌之後，標售與聯準會接力

週二$440億7年期美債標售，接在較弱的5年期結果之後、7月28至29日聯準會決策之前。投資人得知接近40%的7月升息機率是否合理以前，可先取得另一項中段買盤訊號。維持利率但保留9月行動，與更全面的政策風險退卻，意義不同。若下降的是實質殖利率，而非通膨補償再次收窄，才代表債券持有人開始接受能源短期影響之外的較低報酬。

大型科技公司財報，將焦點從AI能否籌得資金，轉向支持融資的現金流。Sopaipilla的7.534%發行殖利率，以及初期約260個基點利差，提供後續交易的具體比較。Nvidia的CDS、保證及客戶融資揭露，將顯示支持較弱對手方，是否增加強勢贊助者的負擔。義務更透明、收入成長可安定持有人；新增承諾則會擴大原已龐大的融資需求。

智利7月28日、英國央行7月30日、日本銀行7月31日接續決策。油價反轉後，智利交換市場仍計入24個月內升息兩次。三家央行指引，以及當地曲線與匯率反應，將顯示先前通膨疑慮還剩多少；日圓接近164兌$1，讓日本判斷尤其受匯率影響。美伊若恢復攻擊，或荷莫茲再受干擾，也會破壞週一債券反彈所依賴的油價緩和。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil plunges, Meta debt rallies and Nvidia's credit risk climbs

## Energy relief reaches bonds, but not real borrowing costs

Treasuries extended their rally on Monday as a pause in US strikes on Iran sent Brent down 9.07% to $88. The 10-year yield fell 4 basis points to 4.65%, outpacing a 2-basis-point decline in the 2-year to 4.31%. Longer bonds led this time, reversing Friday's front-end outperformance and flattening 2s10s to 34 basis points.

The oil retreat did not bring lower real yields. Ten-year inflation compensation fell 5 basis points to 2.21%, more than accounting for the nominal rally, while the real yield edged up to 2.44%. Swaps still assigned almost 40% odds to a July Fed increase, even though almost all surveyed economists expected no change. Investors were shedding some energy risk without abandoning their concern about policy and the cost of capital.

Two AI trades captured the distinction. Sopaipilla's $12.55 billion Meta data-center financing rallied after pricing at a 7.534% yield, resolving Friday's uncertain placement with a substantial concession. Nvidia's five-year default-protection cost, meanwhile, jumped as much as 14 basis points to 82 as potential guarantees and customer financing drew scrutiny. Buyers would fund supported projects at the right price; they were also charging more for the possibility that obligations elsewhere in the AI network would land on a major sponsor's balance sheet.

## Breakevens fall faster than Treasury yields

The US paused strikes after almost two weeks of attacks, Iran refrained from retaliation for a third day, and Oman participated in talks over restoring shipping through Hormuz. WTI fell 8.05% to $82.12. Washington warned that attacks could resume if negotiations failed, leaving the recovery in shipping conditional. Even after Monday's decline, Brent was 22.24% higher over a month and WTI 18.62% higher.

The Treasury rally strengthened from the front end into longer maturities. Five-year yields fell 3 basis points to 4.40%; the 10- and 30-year each declined 4, to 4.65% and 5.12%. Both 2s10s and 2s30s narrowed 2 basis points, finishing at 34 and 81. Yields remained higher over the week by 10, 7, 5 and 1 basis point at two, five, ten and 30 years, and higher over the month by 24, 28, 27 and 25.

Inflation-linked bonds showed how much of the rally depended on oil. The 10-year breakeven's 5-basis-point decline was larger than Friday's 2-basis-point fall. But the real yield rose 1 basis point to 2.44%, leaving it 9 basis points higher over a week and 26 over a month. The fall in expected inflation compensation had yet to translate into a lower real return demanded by bondholders.

Ahead of the July 28–29 Fed meeting, the disagreement between economists and traders remained wide. Hike odds had been near 10% after the July 14 release showed June CPI falling for the first time in six years; they were now almost 40%. Citi's short-rate traders expressed strong conviction in an unchanged decision. Stable employment, effective tariffs and the risk of another energy surge nevertheless sustained the argument for earlier action.

Chairman Kevin Warsh's retreat from forward guidance made the outcome harder to anticipate. Citadel Securities argued that a surprise increase could establish the credibility of genuine data dependence and influence wage and price setting before inflation became entrenched. Other strategists expected a hold that prepared investors for September, by which point markets fully priced an increase. Oil's decline supported patience, but had not settled when officials would respond to the broader inflation risks.

Monday's auctions exposed a narrower difference in demand. The $69 billion 2-year sale attracted solid buying after the recent rise in yields, while the 5-year auction cleared at a higher yield than expected. The softer belly result mattered ahead of Tuesday's $44 billion 7-year sale, where investors would again have to price uncertain policy over a longer holding period. A successful short-note auction did not guarantee the same appetite farther out the curve.

Some investors were already using higher yields to extend duration. State Street's $6 trillion asset-management arm had moved tactically toward longer bonds and credit, despite abandoning an earlier forecast for the 10-year yield to fall toward 3.5% in 2026. Its revised base case put the Fed on hold this year, followed by easing in early 2027 as growth slowed. The position offered income while waiting for that slowdown rather than relying on an immediate policy turn.

Monday improved long-bond marks without erasing their earlier losses. A long-dated Treasury index gained 0.62% but remained down 3.72% over a month; the 30-year yield was still 25 basis points higher over that period. Fiscal borrowing and long corporate issuance continued to compete for investors able to hold duration through the volatility.

## A strong Sopaipilla debut contrasts with Nvidia's CDS jump

Sopaipilla moved from a thin orderbook to a completed deal and an early secondary-market gain. The BlackRock-linked vehicle sold $12.55 billion of investment-grade debt for the Meta campus in El Paso at 7.534%, or 287.5 basis points over Treasuries. The issue was about $273 million larger than initially expected. Orders of $20 billion still covered it only 1.6 times, against roughly four times for investment-grade offerings this year, and pricing did not tighten during syndication.

Early trading then brought the spread to around 260 basis points, about 27.5 tighter than launch. The bonds had offered roughly 40 basis points more than comparable Beignet data-center paper. Sopaipilla holds 80% of the project and Meta 20%; principal amortizes and Meta's leases support payments. The combination of those protections and a high clearing yield attracted buyers even after the weak book. Friday's concern about whether the deal could find support was answered, but at a cost well above what its high-grade rating alone might suggest.

Nvidia's credit protection moved in the opposite direction. Its five-year CDS rose as much as 14 basis points to 82, the largest increase since active trading began in November. Discussions surrounding more than $750 billion of potential AI arrangements included a possible guarantee of up to $250 billion of OpenAI computing leases and potential financing for $350 billion of chip purchases. These were prospective commitments, not completed borrowing, but investors were already considering how much risk could migrate from customers to Nvidia.

Strong sponsors can lower the funding cost of weaker counterparties by backing their obligations. Broadcom's support for much of the previously arranged $35 billion Anthropic financing offered a comparison. Such guarantees can broaden distribution and improve ratings while leaving the sponsor exposed if a customer's cash generation disappoints. Nvidia's CDS increase put a market price on that concern on the same day that Meta-backed cash bonds rallied.

Conventional borrowers still found sizable demand in other markets. AT&T raised €4.7 billion equivalent across four euro tranches ranging from four to 19 years and a £550 million, 26-year sterling bond. It was the first five-tranche European transaction during this seasonally quiet period since at least 2014. Spreads tightened as much as 30 basis points during marketing, ending at 65 over mid-swaps for the four-year tranche and 175 for the longest euro tranche. New-issue concessions of 9.5–19.1 basis points helped place the debt.

AT&T's deal was large relative to the summer calendar: total European corporate, financial and sovereign-related issuance had been only about €5 billion the previous week, and the current week's survey range was €2 billion–€5 billion. Reverse-Yankee issuance had already reached €115 billion in 2026 as US companies sought lower all-in yields and more buyers. European demand was available, even in thin seasonal trading, for an established issuer paying a concession.

At US Renal Care, lenders were seeking the return of collateral rather than just a better price. The company was considering a roughly $2 billion refinancing that would restore assets moved out of existing creditors' reach in a 2023 liability-management transaction. Proposed terms included a $1.2 billion first-lien loan around 500 basis points over benchmarks, $640 million of first-lien notes near an 8% coupon and $350 million of second-lien notes around 11%–12%. The loan and junior notes would be issued at discounts.

The earlier transaction had moved roughly a third of the company's assets. Better operations and a term-loan price near 98 cents, up from 94 at the end of March, now offered a refinancing opportunity. Government-reimbursement exposure and limited free cash flow remained concerns, and the proposal might not proceed. Restoring collateral was part of the proposed bargain for extending maturities at persistently high rates.

Municipal bonds offered another relative-value opportunity after their worst week since April 2025. The 10-year AAA yield reached almost 71% of the comparable Treasury yield, the cheapest ratio since March. The selloff reversed some of the earlier richness created by strong demand for tax-exempt income.

Portfolio diversification was also becoming harder within corporate bonds. Carlyle estimated that investment-grade debt's correlation with US equities had risen from an average 0.13 in 2010–2020 to 0.63 since 2020, while the 100 largest issuers accounted for about 65% of the market. Asset-backed finance could provide different earnings exposures through consumer loans and equipment leases, with junior capital absorbing losses first, although underwriting and structure remained essential to the protection.

Broad credit funds recovered modestly: LQD rose 0.26%, HYG 0.05% and JNK 0.07%. Their monthly returns remained negative at 2.73%, 0.70% and 0.79%, respectively. The Treasury rally helped, but the day's more revealing credit developments were the price needed to place Sopaipilla, Nvidia's prospective obligations and the collateral terms sought at US Renal Care.

## Lower oil does not bring a common central-bank response

German and UK ten-year yields fell 4 and 5 basis points with oil, but ECB Governing Council member Peter Kazimir continued to argue for at least one more rate increase. Even modest improvement in the Middle East would not remove the full energy impact or the risk of second-round effects, he said. Data would have to be unusually convincing for him to abandon September tightening; renewed escalation could require more than one increase over coming quarters. Markets fully priced a quarter-point September move after the ECB's previous hold.

Switzerland's policy baseline was much softer. The SNB's internal expectation was to keep rates at 0% through the end of 2027, absent a new shock, with inflation at 0.5% and forecast to peak at 0.8%, within its 0%–2% target range. Markets nevertheless assigned about 50% odds to an increase in December and fully priced one by March. Energy and currency risks had produced a more hawkish market path than the central bank's inflation forecast implied.

Japan's super-long bonds remained close to record yields. The 40-year had reached 4.01% the previous week, compared with May's 4.355% high, while the yen hovered near 164 per dollar. Persistent inflation, prospective deficits and reduced BOJ buying weighed on demand. Falling approval for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi added concern that further spending or tax relief would increase financing needs.

Higher yields were starting to attract a contrary view. Azimut argued that inflation below 2% made long JGBs appealing at existing levels. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama had urged the $1.81 trillion Government Pension Investment Fund and other large pensions to allocate more domestically. A stronger home bid could stabilize JGBs while retaining savings that otherwise might have gone into Treasuries. Better demand for Japanese bonds would not necessarily mean more Japanese demand for US bonds.

Singapore acted rather than waiting for the oil retreat to settle the inflation outlook. MAS increased the slope of its exchange-rate band for a second consecutive decision, allowing faster currency appreciation. Core inflation was only 1.6%, but the authority expected pressure to build from July as the positive output gap widened to 0.7% of potential GDP and electricity tariffs rose. The Singapore dollar gained 0.15%. The move contrasted with unchanged conventional policy settings in Indonesia and Malaysia and showed the different responses still possible after the common energy shock eased.

## Indonesia's policy shock outweighs the external relief

Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo's resignation, two years before his term ended, interrupted an otherwise favorable day for emerging-market debt. Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti became acting governor. The rupiah fell as much as 0.3%, stocks as much as 0.8%, and the ten-year government yield rose 4 basis points. Protection on Indonesian dollar debt became more expensive, while much of investment-grade Asia outside Japan saw its largest CDS decline in a month as US-Iran tensions eased.

Warjiyo had overseen repeated intervention and 100 basis points of rate increases since May, yet the currency remained near a record low. His departure followed legislation expanding the central bank's remit to growth and employment, amid government pressure to support an 8% growth goal. Fitch, which had already changed the sovereign outlook to negative, warned that diminished perceived independence could raise borrowing costs and erode external buffers. Lower oil was not enough to offset those institutional concerns.

Pakistan had more room to benefit from energy relief. Its central bank held at 11.5%, as 19 of 20 surveyed economists expected, after inflation began easing from a two-year high. An S&P upgrade to B with a stable outlook supported confidence, and the bank projected fiscal 2027 growth of 3.5%–4.5%. More than 90% of the country's energy needs pass through Hormuz, however, leaving that recovery exposed to renewed disruption.

The central bank expected inflation near the upper end of its 5%–7% target range by June 2027. A separate survey was less optimistic, putting fiscal 2027 inflation at 8.5% and growth at 4%. Maintaining rates allowed the bank to wait for clearer evidence that the decline in imported fuel costs would last.

Chile entered its July 28 decision with a sharp policy reversal already embedded in market prices. Against a 4.5% policy rate, two-year rates had risen 47 basis points in 21 days to 4.79%. Swaps shifted from a quarter-point cut to at least one increase over 12 months, while one-year breakevens climbed about 30 basis points in a week to 3.41%, a rise of 123 basis points over a month. June CPI was 4.3%, up from 3.9% and above the 4.1% forecast, so inflation pressure predated the latest oil move.

Chile still placed €3.1 billion across eight-, 12- and 20-year maturities at spreads of 100, 120 and 143 basis points over mid-swaps, substantially inside initial indications. More supply was coming: Congress authorized another $6.2 billion of borrowing and the Finance Ministry planned $5.2 billion of international issuance for the rest of 2026. Debt was projected to peak at 44.2% of GDP in 2029, close to the 45% prudential limit and levels that some analysts linked to downgrade risk.

Venezuela's creditors were organizing ahead of a still-delayed restructuring roadmap. More than 15 funds had joined the committee since January, and the group sought control of as much as half the roughly $60 billion of defaulted sovereign and state oil-company bonds. Its holdings had exceeded $10 billion in 2024. The 2027 bonds traded near 50 cents after gaining more than 60% this year, approaching many recovery estimates even though a sovereign plan had yet to follow the creditor coordination.

Brazil's high carry came with its own fiscal questions. Selic stood at 14.25%, near a two-decade high, alongside a tax burden and debt ratio above many EM peers. XP's founder warned that an uncorrected deficit would eventually return as inflation and higher rates. Net inflows at the platform had fallen 39% from a year earlier despite BRL1.5 trillion of client assets, reflecting the pressure on investors even with high nominal yields available.

Broad external conditions improved: EMB gained 0.34% and a long-duration EM dollar sovereign index 0.56%. With the dollar almost steady, lower oil and Treasury yields helped many borrowers. Indonesia's opposing move showed how quickly local policy credibility could outweigh that relief.

## Technology lags despite the fall in oil

Most US shares advanced, but the largest indices barely benefited from cheaper energy. The S&P 500 rose 0.02%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.32% and semiconductors lost 2.23%. VIX rose 0.48% to 18.67. Doubts over AI spending and its financing remained active, alongside the credit-market scrutiny of guarantees and future debt supply.

The dollar index edged up 0.06% to 101.53, adding little to daily pressure on external borrowers. Gold gained 0.16% despite oil's steep decline, as negotiations and shipping remained uncertain. Markets welcomed de-escalation without treating it as a completed settlement, while technology's losses kept lower nominal yields from translating into a broad risk rally.

## Auctions and the Fed follow a sharp commodity reversal

Tuesday's $44 billion 7-year Treasury sale follows a weaker 5-year auction and precedes the July 28–29 Fed decision. It will provide another reading of demand in the belly before investors learn whether almost 40% July hike odds were justified. A hold that leaves September action open would differ materially from a broader retreat in policy risk. Falling real yields, rather than another decline in breakevens alone, would show that bondholders were accepting lower returns beyond the immediate oil effect.

Upcoming megacap results turn the focus from the availability of AI financing to the cash flows supporting it. Sopaipilla's 7.534% launch yield and early spread near 260 basis points provide a concrete comparison for subsequent deals. Nvidia's CDS and disclosures on guarantees or customer financing will show whether support for weaker counterparties is adding to the perceived burden on stronger sponsors. More transparent obligations and revenue growth could reassure holders; additional commitments would add to the financing pipeline they already have to absorb.

Chile decides policy on July 28, followed by the BOE on July 30 and BOJ on July 31. Chilean swaps included two increases over 24 months despite the oil reversal. Guidance from all three banks, and the response of local curves and currencies, will show how much of the earlier inflation concern survives. Japan's yen near 164 per dollar makes that assessment particularly sensitive to exchange rates. Any renewed attacks or disruption around Hormuz would also undermine the commodity relief on which Monday's bond gains rested.
